papers.title: One-Entry Golden Seamless Cloning with a Reusable Donor Streamlines Plant Gene Functional Analysis
papers.abstract: Molecular cloning underpins functional genomics, yet current toolboxes force a trade-off. Golden Gate frameworks handle one-pot multi-fragment assembly but overcomplicate routine single-gene cloning, whereas Gibson, In-Fusion, and Gateway systems need backbone linearization, resequencing, or proprietary recombinases that leave scars. Here we present Golden Seamless (GS), a one-entry, many-destination system in which a single PCR captures a gene once into a reusable Entry-and-Expression Clone that is never re-cloned. Circle-to-circle Golden Gate moves the same validated clone into plant, yeast, or bacterial vectors without linearization, and a ccdB counter-selection with orthogonal antibiotic markers drives background near zero. Bacterial destinations embed superfolder GFP, enabling naked-eye monitoring of recombinant proteins and an antibody-free dual-modality EMSA that resolves protein and DNA channels across a >150-nm spectral gap. GS thus consolidates capture, distribution, and validation into one low-background workflow with built-in quality control, cutting the time and cost of screening many candidates across functional assays.

papers.title: Engineered regulatory states resolve context-dependent genetics in macular degeneration
papers.abstract: The effects of many genes and disease-associated variants remain hidden in standard cellular models, limiting functional interpretation. Here we engineer regulatory states via CRISPR activation of transcription factors (TFs) in human RPE-1 cells, a model for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Multiome Perturb-seq profiling of single-TF perturbations identified regulators that selectively opened chromatin at AMD GWAS variants inaccessible in resting RPE-1. Priming of partner motifs in chromatin made accessible by single-TF perturbations predicted TF pairs generating emergent transcriptional states in combinatorial Perturb-seq, providing a design principle for selecting informative interactions. Distinct TF pairs also showed variable convergence between polygenic AMD signals and Mendelian retinal disease genes, supporting an omnigenic model shaped by regulatory states. Finally, Mosaic, a chromatin-informed model of TF interaction phenotypes, nominated out-of-sample regulators, including a higher-order combination with experimentally validated emergent effects on AMD-associated programs. Engineered regulatory states thus bring hidden disease biology within experimental reach.

papers.title: Evolution of novel host-microbiota coupling underlies adaptation to nutrient-scarce environments.
papers.abstract: Animals colonizing food-limited environments need to overcome growth constraints by adapting to low, inconsistent nutritional inputs. Comparative studies of surface and cave populations of the Mexican tetra fish species Astyanax mexicanus provide a powerful system to explore evolution to food scarcity. In nutrient-scarce caves, evolved traits such as eye loss and increased fat storage have been shown to conserve energy in cavefish1-3 . However, the role of microbiota-mediated metabolism in sustaining growth and survival under food limitation remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that surface and cave populations distinctly modulate their gut microbiota, with cavefish recruiting microbes whose predicted metabolites specifically promote growth under nutrient-limited conditions. Using microbiota data from three distinct dietary regimes and a fasting treatment, integrated topological data analysis4 and sparse modeling identify sugar and fatty acid degradation pathways coupled with growth in cavefish. Notably, the metabolites of these pathways are beneficial only for cavefish growth, and not for surface fish. Fasting in cavefish led to the recruitment of gut microbes capable of metabolizing aromatic compounds inaccessible to the host, whereas it recruited few microbial associates in surface fish. Our findings indicate that cavefish evolved novel host-microbiota coupling to sustain growth and resilience in their nutrient-scarce niche. We anticipate that our findings will broadly inform studies of evolution under extreme nutritional conditions and provide insights into the role of host-microbiota interactions in resilience to food scarcity at varied time scales.

papers.title: 2C-RT Quantifies Genome-Wide DNA Replication Perturbationsand Redefines RIF1-CDC7 Regulation of Replication Timing
papers.abstract: Replication timing (RT) coordinates DNA synthesis with genome organization and influences mutation rates, cancer evolution, and developmental plasticity. Current methods infer S-phase timing from DNA content, an assumption that obscures responses to replication perturbations and limits accurate comparisons of RT changes. Here, we develop 2C-RT, a multiplexed sequencing approach that uses DNA content-independent markers for robust RT profiling across S phase. Combining 2C-RT with imaging, we resolve distinct layers of human RT control and identify local and genome-wide responses to drugs and genetic perturbations. We find that RIF1 spatially restricts CDC7 activity and that its loss does not neutralize RT per se but advances replication across most RIF1-sensitive regions. A conserved MCM5 bob1 mutation lowers the origin-activation threshold and reveals a role for CDC7 in establishing local origin dominance. These findings support a revised model in which CDC7 primes early origins, CDK promotes permissive origin firing genome-wide, and RIF1 counteracts CDC7 in distinct chromatin states and peripheral nuclear domains.

papers.title: Interdependent mode of RNA recognition by the interacting KH-domain proteins KhpA and KhpB
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are central regulators of gene expression. In bacteria, two KH domain-containing proteins, KhpA and KhpB, are increasingly recognized as globally-acting RBPs, including in pathogens that lack well-studied RBPs, such as Hfq and ProQ. While KhpA and KhpB interact with various RNAs in diverse bacteria, their crosstalk and molecular basis of RNA recognition remain poorly understood. Here, we explored the mutual dependence between KhpA and KhpB in the food-borne pathogen Campylobacter jejuni. We demonstrate KhpA and KhpB interact in vivo, and their individual global RNA recognition is largely dependent on the presence of the partner protein. Using RNA co-immunoprecipitation, we reveal that KhpA requires a conserved KH domain motif for RNA binding, whereas KhpB relies on an atypical R3H domain. Moreover, mutating the RNA-binding domain of one protein compromises the RNA interactome of the other. Overall, we demonstrate an interdependent RNA-binding mode of KhpA and KhpB and anticipate that such KH-proteins have co-evolved to elicit joint RNA regulation in bacteria.

papers.title: Mechanistic prediction of fecal microbiota transplant engraftment and Clostridioides difficile colonization resistance with μODE
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomics routinely resolves microbial community composition down to the strain level via metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), but translating these static catalogs into mechanistic, time-resolved understandings of ecosystem dynamics remains a critical computational bottleneck. Here, we present muODE, a fully automated framework that converts MAGs into dynamical simulations of community metabolism equipped with a composable, literature-grounded ecology layer, fundamentally designed to serve as a mechanistic hypothesis-testing engine. It employs dynamic flux balance analysis (dFBA) coupled to a shared extracellular pool and integrates a composable ecology layer capturing pH inhibition, time-varying antibiotic pharmacokinetics, bile-acid transformations, and spore dormancy. To evaluate the core engine, we cross-validated the dFBA machinery to machine precision against an independent reference implementation. We provide native export to the established COMETS engine for third-party verification. Benchmarking against two independent experimentally validated datasets confirmed that while monoculture growth is robustly captured, overflow secretion and directed community composition remain strictly bounded by the flux-routing limitations of max-biomass FBA. However, when applied to rate-modifying ecological feedback, muODE mechanistically and quantitatively reproduces bile-acid-mediated colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile. With a single rate parameter calibrated so that baseline deoxycholate matched its measured physiological concentration, the framework reproduced the uncalibrated antibiotic-induced collapse of deoxycholate, with the calibrated inhibitor concentration coinciding with the independently set inhibitory threshold of the pathogen and driving a ~44x shift in the simulated pathogen-susceptibility ratio; bile-acid transformation is represented in the composable ecology layer rather than in the genome-scale stoichiometry. Finally, applying muODE end-to-end to a real longitudinal fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) yielding 139 de novo genome-scale metabolic models, the framework successfully recovered the clinical direction of treatment. By transparently diagnosing the structural competitive-exclusion bias that limits precise compositional prediction, muODE motivates the necessity of community-objective extensions while transitioning microbiome modeling from descriptive taxonomy toward testable, quantitatively-validated dynamic hypothesis testing, laying the essential mechanistic groundwork for the predictive engineering of safe, targeted ecological therapeutics. muODE is freely available at https://github.com/cumbof/muODE.

papers.title: Mice immunized with N1 neuraminidase in a single cycle infectious virus or in a recombinant nanoparticle vaccine are protected against lethal challenge with highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 influenza
papers.abstract: The recent spillover of highly pathogenic (HP) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into dairy cattle and other mammalian species has been concerning. Vaccine candidates that can be rapidly synthesized and implemented are key countermeasures for protecting the human population against emerging pathogens. Here we examine the use of a pH1N1 virus lacking the genetic material for hemagglutinin (HA), limiting the infection to a single cycle (sciIAV) or Cobalt lipid-porphyrin nanoparticles decorated with neuraminidase (NA) of HPAI H5N1 (N1-CoPoP) as vaccine candidates. C57BL/6 mice that were inoculated intranasally with a single dose of pH1N1 sciIAV did not differ in serum NA antibody compared to uninoculated mice. However, mice that were inoculated intramuscularly with the N1-CoPoP alone or in combination with pH1N1 sciIAV had increased N1 IgG antibodies. Upon lethal challenge with HPAIV H5N1, all mice inoculated with either pH1N1 sciIAV or N1-CoPoP were protected from weight loss, unlike unvaccinated mice with substantial body weight losses that succumb to viral infection between 7 and 10 days post infection (dpi). Both pH1N1 sciIAV and N1-CoPoP immunization minimized viral infection such that only one mouse receiving pH1N1 sciIAV had detectable viral titer in the lungs at 4 dpi. By 6 dpi, no mouse inoculated with pH1N1 sciIAV and/or N1-CoPoP had detectable virus in nasal turbinates, lungs or the brain, unlike the high viral titers found in uninoculated mice. Both pH1N1 sciIAV and N1-CoPoP were protective and should be investigated further as alternative vaccine candidates.

papers.title: A conditional upper-bound design map for rhodopsin-augmented electro microbial CO2-to-biomass conversion
papers.abstract: The value of rhodopsin proton pumps as light harvesters in electro-microbial CO2-to-biomass conversion depends on molecular photophysics, pathway energetics and reactor light delivery. We couple these scales for Cupriavidus necator, comparing Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) and reductive glycine (rGlyP) assimilation. The model predicts a 17.9% dark rGlyP yield advantage, close to 16.5% measured in chemostats. At 568 nm, 100 PPFD and 45% membrane occupancy, light-derived ATP raises yield by 17% for rGlyP and 14% for CBB. Charging CO2 capture and formate electrosynthesis, a retinal-only reactor reaches 3.29% efficiency versus 2.56% in the dark. A carotenoid antenna raises this to 3.52% at the model-derived 70% transfer estimate and helps in 93.2% of uncertainty samples, but lowers efficiency at the thermodynamic limit by diverting photons from photovoltaics. Point-source CO2 cuts the relative light benefit from 38% to 8%. Rhodopsin is therefore most useful when upstream formate is energy-intensive, not as a general efficiency boost.

papers.title: Engineering the NAT-ULT module increases seed number per pod in soybean
papers.abstract: Seed number per pod is a major soybean yield-component trait, yet experimentally validated causal modules remain poorly defined. Here, we identify and functionally validate a soybean NAT-ULT regulatory module controlling ovule and seed number per pod. Through a visual screen of a fast-neutron-irradiated Glycine max cv. Williams 82 population, we isolated MO27, which increased four-seeded pod frequency from approximately 2-4% in wild type to 27-30%, without major changes in plant architecture, total pod number, or seed morphology. Comparative genome hybridization mapped the phenotype to a 46.7-kb chromosome 2 deletion containing GmNAT1 and chromosome 6 deletions encompassing GmULT-B1 and GmULT-B3. Ovule-clearing analysis showed that increased seed number originated before fertilization through elevated formation of four-ovule ovaries. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis of GmNAT1, GmULT-B1, and GmULT-B3 increased four-seeded pod frequency without detectable penalties in 100-seed weight, total pod number, or plant height. Tomato SlULT triple mutants also increased floral organ and locule number, supporting conserved ULT-like function in reproductive organ patterning. RNA-seq interaction analysis revealed a chromosome 6-dominant transcriptional state, accompanied by selective non-additive reprogramming of hormone/ovule-number and cell-wall-remodeling modules. Integrated genetic and transcriptomic analyses support a hierarchical model in which NAT-ULT perturbation may enhance meristematic competence and remodel reproductive developmental programs, while additional fast-neutron-background-associated transcriptional changes may further modulate the phenotype. These findings define NAT-ULT as a molecular target for engineering soybean seed number per pod.

papers.title: Malignant and stromal partial EMT programmes and cetuximab outcome in head and neck cancer
papers.abstract: Partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEMT) was defined in single malignant cells of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma but is usually scored in bulk tumours. In three single-cell datasets, its laminin-332 and hemidesmosome genes were expressed by malignant cells (the malignant arm) and its fibrillar collagens and vimentin by fibroblasts (the stromal arm). In bulk tumours the stromal arm dominated co-expression, so standard pEMT scores mainly measure stroma. We recovered the malignant arm with a classifier trained on single cells and a 12-gene core. In 40 patients treated with platinum and cetuximab, both malignant measures were higher in those with long progression-free survival (area under the curve 0.78 and 0.82), and the stromal arm was not. The malignant arm was inseparable from the Basal subtype, whose score did as well or better in these patients (0.93) and in two xenograft panels. Bulk pEMT scores should be read by cell of origin.

papers.title: Efficacy of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) in triple negative breast cancer cells and synergy with PARP inhibitor talazoparib
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is the most diagnosed cancer worldwide. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a subtype with a poor prognosis because of its aggressiveness and high likelihood of relapse, making its treatment particularly challenging. We explored the effect of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) as a novel treatment option for breast cancer, which can be used together with other therapies, such as PARP inhibitors. TTFields use alternating electric fields to inhibit cell growth and induce cellular damage. Our findings indicate that TTFields increase expression of the universal cell cycle CDK inhibitory protein p21(WAF1)/CDKN1A independently of TP53 mutational status. Moreover, when used together with the PARP inhibitor talazoparib, the combination further upregulates p21 protein. Both TTFields alone and together with talazoparib induce cell death as documented by PARP cleavage while reducing markers of cell growth and anti-apoptotic proteins, including p-STAT3, STAT3, and MCL-1. Additionally, TTFields together with talazoparib induce DNA damage, as indicated by increased {gamma}H2AX expression. The combination of talazoparib plus TTFields treatment decrease PDL-1 levels and given its utility in predicting response to PD-1/PD-L1 by mediating immune evasion, this raises the possibility of future combination for immune modulation in cancer therapy. Our preclinical results suggest TTFields alone or together with PARP inhibitors such as talazoparib as a promising therapeutic approach for further development for the treatment of breast cancer.

papers.title: Reduced emerin expression marks gastric cancer progression and invasive nuclear remodeling
papers.abstract: Altered nuclear morphology is a defining diagnostic feature of malignancy, and nuclear structure is increasingly recognized as a functional regulator of cancer cell invasion. The inner nuclear membrane protein emerin maintains nuclear architecture and restrains invasive phenotypes in breast cancer models, but whether emerin expression is similarly altered in gastric cancer has not been established. Here, we analyzed emerin protein expression, nuclear morphology, and impeded migration in nonmalignant and malignant gastric cell lines. In parallel, emerin protein expression and nuclear envelope localization across gastric cancer was determined using patient tissue microarrays. Emerin was abundant at the nuclear envelope in cancer-adjacent and noncancerous gastric epithelium but was reduced across multiple gastric cancer histologies, including adenocarcinoma, signet-ring cell carcinoma, mucinous adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and metastatic lesions. Reduced emerin at the nuclear envelope was most strongly associated with higher-grade tumors, with grade 2 and grade 3 cancers exhibiting significantly lower nuclear envelope scores than noncancerous tissue and grade 1 tumors. Consistent with the patient tissue data, the gastric cancer cell lines AGS and MKN1 expressed less emerin protein than noncancerous gastric epithelial control cells HFE-145. Consistent with studies in breast cancer cells, gastric cells with reduced emerin expression also had smaller nuclei and increased impeded migration through 8 micron pores. These findings support a model in which reduced nuclear envelope emerin is a conserved feature of invasive epithelial tumor progression and a candidate biomarker of gastric cancer nuclear remodeling.

papers.title: Positive selection and structural disruption of KCNA5 by mutation in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Ion channels regulate cell proliferation, survival and migration, but the functional consequences of many ion channel mutations in cancer are unknown, and electrophysiological characterisation at scale is impractical. Here we use the mutational landscape of colorectal adenocarcinoma as a functional filter to identify potassium channel mutations under selection. A dN/dS screen of 16 potassium channels expressed in the large intestine identified KCNA5 (Kv1.5) as the strongest candidate under positive mutational selection. These mutations cluster in the T1 tetramerisation, S1-S4 voltage-sensor and pore domains, yet avoid the selectivity filter, indicating that selection does not favour loss of conduction. Within the pore region, the observed mutations occupy a biophysical space distinct from known C-type inactivation, activation-gate and toxin-binding mutations. In the voltage sensor, mutations affect gating-charge arginines. In the T1 domain, mutations fall on inter-subunit interfaces conserved across the KCNA family, and saturation mutagenesis energy calculations predict that they destabilise subunit contacts or the folding of the domain. Molecular dynamics simulations of D166N and G128R show loss of coordinated interface dynamics and distortion of the local backbone, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis of KCNA5-mutant tumours shows reduced expression of cell-cycle, KRAS-related and inflammatory pathways, and we observe differences between transcriptional effects induced by T1 and S1-S4 domain mutations. These changes are not reproduced by low KCNA5 expression alone, consistent with an effect specific to the mutant protein. Together, these computational results highlight that KCNA5 is under mutational selection in colorectal adenocarcinoma, and that these mutations are likely functional and induce phenotypic effects on tumors.

papers.title: A reference-calibrated spatial-statistical framework for quantifying stroma-tumor cell spatial associations from histology and its geometric limits
papers.abstract: Quantifying interactions in biological tissues requires determining whether an interaction exists, the distance over which it operates, and its strength. Existing spatial-statistical approaches can characterize spatial organization but often require interaction range or interaction models to be specified a priori, making them less suited to settings where these quantities are themselves unknown. Here, we present a practical framework that recovers the presence, range, and association strength of spatial bias toward a tissue structure directly from segmented histology. The framework combines four complementary statistics, the resource selection function, nearest-structure distance distributions, the cross J-function, and the radial distribution function, with specimen-specific reference states that preserve tissue stromal architecture while spanning a continuum of known spatial biases. Across controlled in silico tissues, we show that tissue stromal architecture imposes geometric limits on the range of recoverable interactions and that event fraction independently constrains statistical sensitivity. These spatial associations establish fundamental bounds on inference and demonstrate that spatial statistics must be interpreted relative to tissue-specific reference states rather than absolute scales. We apply the framework to proliferating tumor cells relative to CAF-rich stroma during tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy in an ALK+ NSCLC model and identify a strong stroma-associated proliferation bias extending approximately 30-60 micrometers. The framework broadly applies to any histological setting where events and reference structures can be defined, providing a practical approach to quantify localized interactions directly from tissue stromal architecture.

papers.title: Radiotherapy Reshapes the 3D Genome in Medulloblastoma Cells
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is central to medulloblastoma treatment, yet the molecular and three-dimensional (3D) genome responses to irradiation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated RNA sequencing, proteomics, and Micro-C to characterise the response of ONS-76 medulloblastoma cells to clinically relevant radiation exposures. A single 2 Gy dose induced widespread transcriptional and proteomic changes, including altered cell adhesion, migration, DNA replication, and ribosome biogenesis pathways. Integrated analysis identified LAMB3 and AKR1B10 as candidate mediators of radioresponse that remained elevated following fractionated irradiation. Micro-C profiling following single and repeated 2 Gy exposures revealed radiation-induced 3D genome remodelling. While global genome organisation remained largely stable, irradiation promoted shifts towards active A compartments, new TAD boundary formation, and transient boundary strengthening. Together, these findings provide the first genome-wide characterisation of radiation-induced 3D chromatin reorganisation in a medulloblastoma model and identify molecular and structural features associated with radioresponse.

papers.title: Developmental rewiring of EHMT1 function during human cortical neurogenesis
papers.abstract: Ubiquitously expressed chromatin regulators orchestrate cell-type-specific gene expression programs, yet how they acquire distinct regulatory functions during development remains fundamentally unresolved. Using temporally controlled protein depletion during human cortical neurogenesis in vitro, we show that the autism-associated histone methyltransferase EHMT1 is developmentally repurposed from epiblast to cortical neurons. Broadly expressed zinc finger proteins recruit EHMT1 to distinct cis-regulatory elements within changing chromatin landscapes associated with lineage-specific transcription factor activity, with extensive remodeling of EHMT1 enhancer occupancy during neural induction dependent on ZNF462. This genomic rewiring is accompanied by a fundamental shift from restraining premature developmental gene expression in pluripotent cells to supporting neuronal programs, with distinct transcriptional consequences of EHMT1 loss across neural progenitors and excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes. Timed depletion and recovery experiments identify the neural progenitor stage as the onset of a developmental period during which EHMT1 is required for faithful neuronal maturation. Remarkably, EHMT1 can re-engage stage-specific targets after prolonged deficiency, allowing extensive transcriptional recovery with only limited molecular scarring. These findings reveal how ubiquitous epigenetic machinery acquires developmental specificity while demonstrating the resilience of developmental gene regulatory programs to prolonged disruption, with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Spatial proteomics identifies altered thick ascending limb cells as drivers of kidney disease through uromodulin retention
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasingly prevalent and is a leading cause of mortality. Recent transcriptomic studies have identified the persistence of injury-induced renal tubular epithelial cell states, yet the cell populations that drive CKD remain unresolved. Uromodulin (UMOD) is the most abundant urinary secreted protein expressed exclusively in thick ascending limb (TAL) epithelial cells in the kidney. UMOD is strongly associated with CKD risk in genome-wide association studies, suggesting a broader, yet unexplored role of UMOD and TAL cells in CKD pathogenesis. Here, using spatial proteomics, we identified an injury-induced TAL cell state marked by intracellular UMOD accumulation. Spatially resolved multimodal integration revealed that UMOD accumulation occurred without transcriptional upregulation. Impaired urinary UMOD secretion further supported pathological intracellular retention. These altered TAL cells with UMOD retention exhibited inflammatory signaling, formed profibrotic niches enriched with M2-like macrophages across renal compartments, and were associated with CKD progression in multiple experimental models. Reducing the burden of UMOD retention diminished altered TAL cells and their profibrotic microenvironments, and attenuated CKD development. A similar altered TAL state was identified in human kidney disease and was associated with worse kidney function. Together, we identify pathological UMOD retention and altered TAL cells as key drivers of CKD development and potential therapeutic targets. This study also highlights that protein-level alterations can redefine disease-associated cell states beyond transcript profiling.

papers.title: Single-Cell Proteo-Transcriptomic Profiling Uncovers Post-Translational Regulatory Layers in Human Hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: Background: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) have the unique ability to produce all mature cell types in the blood and understanding the mechanisms governing their differentiation and renewal is a driving question in stem cell biology. While single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our view of human hematopoiesis, mRNA abundance represents an incomplete proxy for functional cell states. Here, we apply single-cell multimodal profiling to simultaneously measure 280 surface and intracellular protein targets alongside whole transcriptomes within individual adult human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Results: By directly coupling modalities within single cells, we show that protein-RNA correlations peak dynamically in transitioning intermediate progenitors across lineages, consistent with pervasive post-transcriptional mechanics underlying lineage choice. Furthermore, key transcription factor proteins maintain multilineage co-expression longer into commitment than their transcripts, demarcating a possible window of fate decision reversibility. Moreover, low and flat CTNNB1 mRNA levels mask late-erythroid {beta}-catenin protein enrichment, apparently pairing with E-cadherin expression and suggesting post-translational stabilization at the cell membrane. Conclusions: This dataset enables the observation of translational dynamics and RNA-protein relationships throughout the differentiation landscape at an unprecedented level of granularity. Together, our findings demonstrate that transcriptomics alone misses fundamental regulatory programs, establishing single-cell proteo-transcriptomics as a powerful tool for decoding human stem cell fate.

papers.title: Release of BEC-1 from CED-9 stimulates lysosome tubulation in C. elegans by engaging Class III PI3K complex I
papers.abstract: The anti-apoptotic protein CED-9 and the autophagy protein BEC-1 have been linked to autophagy regulation, but how their interaction modulates this process is not fully understood. Here, we find that the physical dissociation of BEC-1 from CED-9 influences lysosomal morphology in addition to autophagic activity in Caenorhabditis elegans. We present evidence that when autophagy is stimulated via dietary restriction, BEC-1 is released from CED-9 and assembles with VPS-34 and other members of the PI3K complex I to promote PI3P enrichment at lysosomal membranes and subsequent membrane tubulation. Mutation of two hydrophobic amino acids within a predicted BH-3 like motif of BEC-1 is sufficient to disrupt its interaction with CED-9, thereby constitutively inducing lysosomal tubulation and increasing autophagic cargo turnover. This phenotype is dependent on VPS-34 activity, linking the CED-9/BEC-1 dissociation to PI3K-dependent lysosomal remodeling. Collectively, our work identifies the CED-9/BEC-1 interaction as a molecular switch that governs apoptosis, autophagy, and lysosomal morphology.

papers.title: High temperature ligation enables in vitro assembly of eukaryotic genes
papers.abstract: Our ability to efficiently construct synthetic DNA products is essential to studying and engineering biology. There is an abundance of widely adopted DNA assembly technologies suitable for generating synthetic constructs from diverse DNA inputs, but these techniques suffer from low specificity of connection during assembly, which decreases the accuracy, efficiency, and throughput of construction. Here we propose a broadly applicable paradigm for DNA assembly, High Temperature (HighT) assembly, that lowers misconnection rates by ligating complementary single strand DNA overhangs at reaction temperatures significantly higher than their predicted melting temperatures. By expanding the concept of melting temperature to demarcate smaller association fractions of DNA duplexes, we characterize HighT and demonstrate 40 percentage points increase in accuracy, and 4 orders of magnitude increase in yield of transformants when applying the technique to conventional assembly technologies. HighT is then applied to develop cloning pipelines for the development of efficient assembly-to-integration protocols, the construction of specific low-abundance isoforms of medically relevant proteins from human gDNA and oligos, and the de novo construction of a 10 kb, GC rich genomic region from the functionally extinct Northern White Rhinoceros created entirely in vitro.

papers.title: From dynamic transcripts to stable proteins: multi-omics revealed regulatory buffering of Candidatus Accumulibacter under cyclic conditions
papers.abstract: Enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR) relies on polyphosphate-accumulating organisms that experience dynamic fluctuations in redox conditions and substrate availability. How these organisms regulate metabolism across molecular layers under cyclic operation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated molecular regulation in a long-term, stable aerobic granular sludge system dominated by Candidatus Accumulibacter. We combined metagenomics, time-resolved metatranscriptomics, and matched metaproteomics across three consecutive operational cycles. Genome-resolved metagenomics revealed an Accumulibacter-dominated community encoding canonical EBPR functions. Time-resolved metatranscriptomics revealed extensive and reproducible transcriptional dynamics affecting hundreds of genes. These dynamics did not align with discrete EBPR phases or instantaneous environmental transitions, but instead unfolded gradually over the cycle. Despite pronounced transcript-level heterogeneity, aggregation at the functional level revealed strong consolidation, with only a limited number of KEGG orthologs exhibiting coherent temporal regulation. Quantitative metaproteomics revealed a stable proteome across EBPR cycles, with no individual proteins or functional categories showing significant differential abundance despite direct transcript-protein mapping and time-matched sampling. This indicated that transcriptional dynamics did not translate into measurable changes in protein pool size on the time scale of individual cycles, consistent with slow, growth-coupled proteome turnover relative to cycle duration. Together, these results support a hierarchical model of regulation in Candidatus Accumulibacter, in which dynamic transcriptional responses are buffered at both the functional and protein levels. This organization provides a plausible basis for stable EBPR performance under predictable cyclic operation and demonstrates how time-resolved multi-omics can be used to resolve regulatory dynamics across molecular layers in engineered microbial ecosystems.

papers.title: Isoindole-benzohydrazide derivative potentiates colistin activity to overcome resistance conferred by MCR-1 variants in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Polymyxin antibiotic resistance mediated by the mobilized colistin resistance (MCR) enzyme threatens the last-resort treatment of deadly multidrug-resistant pathogens, including Acinetobacter baumannii, and calls for urgent mitigation efforts. We used a multifaceted approach involving computational and wet-lab techniques to identify an isoindole-benzohydrazide derivative, JNAL-042, which potentiates colistin activity in an Escherichia coli MCR-resistance phenotype screening model. JNAL-042 lacked intrinsic antibiotic activity but potentiated that of polymyxin antibiotics at 12-24 mug/ml, as demonstrated by bacterial growth susceptibility screens. Cell viability counts and time-kill assays corroborated these findings, demonstrating complete abolition of MCR-mediated resistance by the antibiotic-adjuvant combination at concentrations mirroring those of empty vector controls. Post-induction treatment with this combination similarly prevented the propagation of the resistance phenotype, albeit at a higher antibiotic dose. This landmark study presents JNAL-042 as a promising antibiotic adjuvant to combat MCR-mediated resistance and offers a viable solution to preserve last-resort polymyxin antibiotics.

papers.title: Circadian phase alignment promotes survival under predictive oxidative stress
papers.abstract: Circadian clocks are endogenous time-keeping mechanisms that continue to oscillate with a period that approximates 24 h in the absence of cyclic environmental cues. This free-running period (FRP) varies from species to species and can vary within species across latitudinal clines. Because natural environments provide daily cues that reset circadian clocks to exactly 24 h, the importance of the FRP length is unclear. Using the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus we show that the FRP length alters the alignment of a biological process with an environmental reference, known as phase angle of entrainment, across seasonal photoperiods, thereby repositioning stress response programs relative to the external environment. This phase relationship affects the overall fitness of the organism: strains that position stress-response programs to peak at the time at which the stressor peaks outcompete their early- or late-peaking counterparts. Our results suggest that the FRP length is selected for its ability to adjust the phase angle of entrainment across seasonal photoperiods: the wild-type FRP length was uniquely plastic in its ability to adjust stress-response programs to coincide with the stressor in all photoperiod conditions.

papers.title: Distribution and dynamics of Vibrio spp. and pathogen sequences among microhabitats and monsoon seasons in Singapore's coastal waters
papers.abstract: Marine infections are rising in temperate regions due in part to a warming climate. However, comparatively little is known about drivers of marine pathogen dynamics in the tropics where temperatures are high year-round. Vibrio bacteria are ubiquitous in both temperate and tropical marine environments, and many are important pathogens of marine organisms and humans. Here, we sampled an equatorial monsoonal site, the Singapore Strait, over 18 months and applied amplicon sequencing (16s rRNA V6-8 region) to three particle size fractions, qPCR quantitation of Vibrio spp., and generalized linear modelling with environmental variables to understand the factors that structure the Vibrio assemblage. We found that Vibrios represented the highest proportion of pathogen-related DNA sequences, with an assemblage composition influenced by microhabitats (size fractions) and monsoon seasons. Vibrio sequences were dominated by ASVs with highest identity to V. xuii, V. rotiferianus and V. caribbeanicus, and including ASVs matching agents of human disease in Singapore - V. parahaemolyticus, V. alginolyticus, and V. furnissii. Vibrio qPCR abundance was lowest in the largest size fraction (10-150 m), following planktonic DNA trends, even though pathogen-related sequences, including Vibrio, were enriched in this fraction. Temperature was a significant predictor of overall Vibrio abundance, but its effect was no longer significant after adjustment for monsoons, suggesting that the temperature association may reflect broader seasonal dynamics. Instead, effects of chlorophyll, ammonia, nitrate and suspended solids were more consistent within seasons. Furthermore, free-living and particle-associated Vibrios responded differently to environmental changes, suggesting that partitioning into microspatial habitats may lead to differences in their environmental sensitivity.

papers.title: Ethnic differences in gut microbiota composition and functional capacity persist over six years in the HELIUS multi-ethnic longitudinal cohort
papers.abstract: Background: Ethnic minority groups in Western Europe carry a disproportionate cardiometabolic disease burden not fully explained by conventional risk factors, and their gut microbiomes differ markedly from those of European-origin populations. Whether these differences persist over time has not been examined prospectively. Results: We followed 1,903 participants from six ethnic groups in the HELIUS cohort over 6 years, using faecal 16S rRNA sequencing across all groups and shotgun metagenomics in a matched Dutch and South-Asian Surinamese subset (N = 238 per group). The extent of microbiota compositional change over time differed between ethnic groups: Moroccan participants showed the largest change, while the Dutch and South-Asian Surinamese participants were most stable. Diabetes mellitus and medication use at baseline were associated with greater compositional drift. However, ethnic differences in composition were largely preserved across all six groups (16S: ethnicity R2 0.044 to 0.037; all 15 pairwise contrasts significant at follow-up) and in the shotgun subset (R2 0.047 to 0.037). At the species level, 61 of 78 ethnicity-associated species remained differentially abundant at follow-up. Alistipes putredinis, the species converging most strongly, was absent at baseline in 43% of South-Asian Surinamese participants, and the convergence was consistent with acquisition of this species by this group. At strain level, within-person strain sharing declined with follow-up duration but was similar between ethnic groups. Within hosts, 90% of A. putredinis populations were retained as the same or a closely related lineage, and within the retained subset, microdiversity increased in both groups. Ethnic differences in functional profiles persisted to a similar extent as those in composition, with limited convergence in fibre-degrading enzyme families (GH5_37, GH26). The total antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) burden in the gut microbiome declined similarly in both groups over time. Dutch participants showed higher baseline ARG diversity that converged toward South-Asian Surinamese levels, while class-level differences were predominantly stable. Conclusions: Six years of follow-up in a shared urban environment narrowed ethnic differences in the gut microbiome only modestly; assuming exponential decline, the observed change corresponds to a half-life of roughly two decades.

papers.title: Pulling water from a stone: subaerial biofilm water dynamics on porous solid materials
papers.abstract: Subaerial biofilms (SABs) are microbial communities that colonize air exposed surfaces in both natural and engineered environments, forming an interface between the atmosphere and the substrate. Often water availability is crucial for their metabolic activity and survival. While precipitation may contribute to SAB hydration, the dynamic processes of evaporation and condensation - closely linked to fluctuating temperature and humidity conditions - can be key determinants of water availability and they constitute the main focus of this study. We present a model connecting the water-related dynamics in an SAB, its surrounding ambient air and underlying stone/masonry. A central feature of the model is the increased water affinity of the SAB in comparison to the stone pore network. Based on thermodynamic principles, the model captures changes in liquid water content and availability by accounting for the evaporation and condensation at liquid-gas interfaces through gradients in water chemical potential. It accounts for the SAB's capacity to delay water loss by drawing water from substrate material pores to compensate for atmospheric evaporation. The proposed model is compared to prior experimental observations of water transport in limestone samples with and without SAB. Additional numerical simulations under variable environmental conditions demonstrate how permeability of the substrate layer may influence SAB water activity, and how the presence or absence of an SAB might affect water content within stone/masonry.

papers.title: Unsupervised decomposition of massively parallel TraDIS-Xpress fitness data from Escherichia coli identifies distinct functional and expression modules of antimicrobial resistance determinants
papers.abstract: Linking genotype to phenotype is a central goal in biology, one way to do this is using transposon insertion sequencing (TIS) where the fitness impacts of mutations across a genome are assessed in different conditions. Traditional analyses use comparison of each gene response independently in control versus test conditions, so a compendium of hundreds of test conditions returns hundreds of separate ranked gene lists. To unlock the potential information hidden within large data sets, we applied independent component (ICA) analysis to 754 Escherichia coli BW25113 TraDIS-Xpress samples. These samples included a series of antibiotic and other stress condition exposures. ICA is designed to identify hidden structure within complex data and to extract meaningfully linked components. In this analysis each annotated gene was resolved into a gene body and 198 bp 5' and 3' features so that expression effects driven by the transposon's outwards facing promoter enter the matrix separately from gene disruption effects. The decomposition returned 99 components, which we term fxModules, which were defined as containing elements with similar responses across the whole compendium rather than per any individual experiment. Of the 754 stress samples, the antibiotic arm included 110 samples derived from exposure to 14 separate agents at multiple concentrations. Many of these have been highly studied allowing us to explore the accuracy of predicted responsive fxModules. This analysis showed excellent predictive power of the approach and the fxModules responsive to individual drugs typically reproduced known mechanisms at a resolution superior to analysis of single gene sets. For example, exposure to fosfomycin identified responsive fxModules containing genes which are known to be involved in uptake of the drug, cAMP-CRP control and exposure to gentamicin identified oxidative phosphorylation split across three fxModules responding with different magnitudes and directions at different concentrations. This recapitulates recent work studying the landscape of E. coli genes sensitive to this drug with high precision without any prior knowledge of functional annotation. Similarly precise predictions were made for other drugs. Responsive modules also identified novel groups of genes and linkages beyond the boundaries of defined pathways as being responsive to various stresses demonstrating the ability to predict new genotype-phenotype links. Inclusion of the regulatory regions also resolved fxModules which were entirely contributed by promoter regions, for example for chloramphenicol genes responsible for efflux were identified by signals in intergenic control regions, and unidirectional insertions in gene bodies, a signal that a gene level matrix would not be able to predict with accuracy. These data show that ICA decomposition provides an efficient and accurate annotation independent approach to identifying sets of genes with related functional impacts in any given condition in the compendium. The functional modular association of genes also help in predicting gene functions of unknown genes based on the group function. This approach allows rapid identification of novel genotype-phenotype links and unlocks the power of multiple comparisons of transposon mutagenesis data.

papers.title: Decision-relevant measurement for precision microbiome interventions
papers.abstract: Human gut microbiome studies often rely on stool, despite increasing evidence that it incompletely represents the spatially heterogeneous intestinal ecosystem. Whether this loss of spatial detail matters for downstream intervention decisions is largely unresolved. We treat compositional reconstruction and decision preservation as separate objectives. Using 16 matched recovery events from 11 participants, each containing stool and four intended regional capsule measurements, we aggregated amplicon sequence variants into 11 prespecified taxonomic and functional proxy guilds. We evaluated models that reconstruct stool from regional measurements by nested leave one participant out validation under complementary compositional geometries. We then assessed decision preservation through three spatial proxy states and measurement induced decision loss (MIDL) across normalized binary intervention thresholds. Multi region CLR ridge and Aitchison models combining regional measurements with a population reference had the lowest point estimate Aitchison errors, but evidence that either outperformed the population Aitchison center was not retained after multiplicity correction. Rankings changed under total variation and after guild amalgamation; at the coarser resolution, the primary ordering showed a small, uncertain reversal that was sensitive to zero handling. The model with the lowest compositional error did not have the lowest MIDL curve calibration error. Population centers closely reproduced the nearly uninformative MIDL curves of observed stool while retaining little individualized regional information. These findings show that reconstruction, decision preservation, and calibration to observed stool decision loss answer different questions. Evaluation of microbiome measurement strategies should therefore treat compositional geometry, biological representation, and the downstream decision task as parts of the estimand.

papers.title: The Human Gut Cell Atlas v1.0: A Unified, Community-BuiltReference of Cellular Diversity Across the Gut
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have transformed our understanding of cellular diversity in the human intestine, but differences in anatomical sampling, experimental processing and cell-type nomenclature limit comparison across datasets. Here, we present the Human Gut Cell Atlas (HGCA) V1, a community-curated reference of 944,390 healthy and disease-adjacent intestinal cells from 502 samples, 265 donors and 24 landmark studies, linked to detailed anatomical, clinical, and technical metadata. As this metadata is of critical importance to human biology, we developed MetaManager, an open source data management framework for standardized metadata collection and tracking. A five-level consensus taxonomy resolves 94 homeostatic cell identities and enables transferrable, high-resolution annotation of new gut datasets. By assembling cell identity, sampling metadata, and independent spatial validation, intestinal segment and radial tissue depth were revealed to systematically shape cellular composition and transcriptional state, enabling inference of the presence of sampling-dependent tissue niches, including lymphoid follicles. Reference mapping accurately and rapidly recovered cohort-level Crohn's disease and treatment signatures without de novo annotation, while mapping human intestinal organoids quantified cell-type-specific identity, regional specification, maturation, and transcriptional fidelity to native tissue. The HGCA V1 provides a standardized cellular, anatomical coordinate, and metadata system for reproducible, high-quality analysis of intestinal biology across healthy tissue, disease-associated remodelling, and experimental models, providing a continuously evolving community reference for cumulative discovery in human intestinal biology.

papers.title: Modular Cell-Free Extract Mixing Enables Soluble, Active Biomanufacturing of Difficult-to-Express and Aggregation-Prone Proteins
papers.abstract: Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) is a powerful platform for rapid protein prototyping and biomanufacturing, but expression of complex proteins remains limited by labor-intensive extract preparation as well as the inability of conventional Escherichia coli extracts to efficiently support disulfide bond formation and prevent protein aggregation. We previously developed a Cell-Free Autoinduction (CFAI) workflow that simplifies extract preparation, however, CFAI-derived extracts retain the folding limitations of standard E. coli systems for producing traditionally difficult proteins. Here, we address these challenges by utilizing extracts enriched with molecular chaperones or Erv1p-based oxidative folding catalysts and combining them through a modular extract mixing strategy to enable independent tuning of the cell-free folding environment. This workflow supplies folding factors through enriched extracts, avoiding recurring purchases of purified supplements and enabling a modeled reagent-cost advantage. To evaluate real-world applications and utility of lysate mixing for protein production, we demonstrate a 10-fold increase in solubility of the aggregation-prone bacterial toxin Colicin M, achieving >95% soluble protein while retaining antimicrobial activity. We further used a Design of Experiments (DoE) framework to optimize combinations of chaperone-enriched and Erv1p-based oxidative folding extracts containing either protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) or DsbC. The optimized compositions produced >95% soluble truncated human tissue plasminogen activator (vtPA), comprising the kringle 2 and protease domains, while preserving enzymatic activity. Together, these results demonstrate that CFAI-derived modular extract mixing provides a tunable, high-throughput strategy with low modeled materials costs for tailoring cell-free biochemical environments for difficult-to-express proteins, expanding CFPS utility for protein engineering and biomanufacturing.
